# research/

<!-- Generated by research/_index.py; do not edit by hand. Edit the script, then run it. -->

Work that is not a single cipher target: the archive sweeps that look for new ciphers, the passes that vet what they find, and a few surveys and analyses. One folder per piece of work, 229 in all, 194 of them sweeps. This file lists each folder once.

## Start here

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`SWEEP.md`](SWEEP.md) | The brief a contributor gives their own AI agent to run one sweep: read what has been searched, choose an archive, search, write the folder. |
| [`VET.md`](VET.md), [`vet.py`](vet.py) | The brief a contributor gives their agent to vet leads already found, the list of leads waiting (`--list`) and the check of a vetting file (`--check`). |
| [`COVERAGE.md`](COVERAGE.md) | What has **not** been swept yet, by area and archive. Pick a sweep from it; remove the row when a sweep closes it. |
| [`leads.json`](leads.json) | Every lead the sweeps found that is not yet vetted into `catalogue.json`. Written by `merge.py`, never by hand. |
| [`archive_sweep_2026-10/BRIEF.md`](archive_sweep_2026-10/BRIEF.md) | What counts as a lead, and the row a sweep writes for each one (`candidates.json`). |
| [`archive_sweep_2026-10/known.py`](archive_sweep_2026-10/known.py) | `python known.py "<shelfmark or name>"`: is this item already in the catalogue, the leads, the notes or DECODE? Run it before writing a row. |
| [`vetting_2026-11/BRIEF.md`](vetting_2026-11/BRIEF.md) | How a lead is vetted before it can enter the catalogue (the vetting bar is in the README Conventions). |

A lead goes from a sweep to the catalogue in four steps: the sweep writes `<folder>/candidates.json`; `python research/archive_sweep_2026-10/merge.py --write` merges it into `leads.json`; a vetting pass fills the lead's `vetting` block; `python docs/_check_catalogue.py --promote <id>` moves it to `catalogue.json`. A contributor's agent does the first step from [`SWEEP.md`](SWEEP.md) or the third from [`VET.md`](VET.md), and sends its folder as a pull request ([CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md), "Searching an archive with your AI").

## A sweep folder

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | What was searched (portal, terms, date), what was found, what was blocked and what is left. A sweep that found nothing still keeps this, so the next one does not repeat it. |
| `candidates.json` | One row per lead, in the BRIEF schema. `[]` is a valid result. |
| `coverage.md`, `key_leads.json` | Optional: series looked at page by page; bare keys found on the way. |
| scripts, `hits.jsonl`, logs | The harvest as it was run. Page images and downloads stay out of git. |

Folder names are historical and are cited by path from `merge.py`, `COVERAGE.md`, the leads and the target notes, so folders are not renamed. A new sweep is named `sweep_<yyyy-mm-dd>_<archive or area>`; after adding one, run `python research/_index.py`.

## Sweeps, by area

"Rows" is the number of leads in the folder's `candidates.json` (0 = searched, nothing kept; a dash = the sweep kept its finds elsewhere, see its README). Oldest first within an area.
